findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [confidence 100, P1] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` applies a numeric cursor codec to the endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"`, so optimized pagination over any nonempty audit-log result raises TypeError while generating cursors, and `return cursor.value` also removes DateTimePaginator's timestamp decoding for existing cursor values.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. In the OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() method at lines 878-883, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (a negative value) and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and will raise an AssertionError or similar exception. The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' but this is false - Django explicitly does not support negative indexing on QuerySets. This is a real bug that would cause an unhandled exception when the advertised negative-offset feature is used.
